qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Canadian Big Six banking oligopoly protected by OSFI regulatory barriers, Bank Act foreign ownership limits, and Canada's largest low-cost core retail deposit base (~C$500B+). Delivers persistent 14-17% multi-cycle ROE with unmatched domestic scale and pricing power in fee-based wealth management and retail banking. Primary erosion risks: Canadian residential mortgage credit cycle deterioration, OSFI regulatory capital increases, open banking mandates, and fintech payments disintermediation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (REJECT). While Royal Bank of Canada is Canada's preeminent financial institution with an exceptional ~16% multi-cycle ROE and elite stewardship, as a fractional-reserve commercial deposit-taking bank it structurally fails the Munger Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency standard. Operating at ~16-17x asset/equity leverage ($2.0T+ assets vs ~$115B equity) and funded by demand deposits, its solvency inherently relies on depositor confidence, wholesale liquidity, and central bank/CDIC backstops ('kindness of strangers'). Free cash conversion cannot be evaluated independently of regulatory capital requirements (RWA growth).
qualitative.evidence: Canadian banking oligopolist (#1 domestic market share in retail deposits, mortgages, and wealth management). Demonstrates multi-cycle ROE consistently between 14-17% (5-year median ~15%) and disciplined capital stewardship under CEO Dave McKay (e.g. non-dilutive C$13.5B acquisition of HSBC Canada). However, Gate 6 structural rejection is absolute for commercial fractional-reserve deposit banks: total balance sheet liabilities exceed C$1.9T against CET1 capital ratio of ~13.0%, with balance sheet leverage exceeding 16x. Funding model relies on short-duration demand deposits and wholesale capital market facilities to support long-duration residential mortgages and commercial credit, subjecting equity to asset-liability duration mismatch and credit cycle tail risk.
